title: How Cigna's AI chief is investing in the technology to cut costs and address some of healthcare's biggest problems
summary: Cigna's chief data, digital, and AI officer, Katya Andresen, is shifting the company's focus from merely using AI to leading in an age of AI, aiming to measure its impact on health outcomes. Cigna projects its AI and predictive analytics tools will save an estimated $200 million over three years by proactively connecting patients with clinicians, and has invested $100 million to reduce clinician documentation time and speed up prescription processes. Andresen emphasizes AI's role in personalizing healthcare, making it more conversational, ambient, and proactive, while leveraging proprietary data and partnerships with major AI players to develop competitive tools.

summary: Teledyne LeCroy has launched the OakGate R300-G6-PRO and DE200-G6-PRO PCIe 6.0 NVMe SSD Validation Platforms, which are the first native end-to-end PCIe 6.0 solution for NVMe SSDs. summary: Medical device maker Boston Scientific has reported a "global disruption" to its operations due to an ongoing cyberattack that began on Tuesday. The incident has affected its IT systems, limiting access to information systems and business applications, and impacting its ability to process and ship customer orders. The company is investigating with third-party experts, but currently has no timeline for full restoration, and the full extent of operational and financial impacts remains unknown, causing its shares to drop.

title: Florence police make arrest in alleged $80K Duke Energy equipment theft
summary: Florence police arrested Charles McGee Jr., 30, for allegedly stealing $80,000 worth of Duke Energy equipment, including a boat and copper wire, between August 10 and August 25. McGee faces charges of 3rd-degree burglary, grand larceny, transportation of stolen nonferrous metals, and possession with intent to distribute methamphetamine. He is currently held at the Florence County Detention Center awaiting a bond hearing.

title: Live Nation Antitrust Lawsuit: Trump Wanted Your Tickets to Be Expensive
summary: A recent article by Madiba K. Dennie details how former President Donald Trump allegedly interfered in the Justice Department's antitrust lawsuit against Live Nation Entertainment. Despite the Biden administration's efforts to break up the Live Nation-Ticketmaster monopoly, Trump reportedly directed the DOJ to settle the case after a meeting with Live Nation's CEO. This interference, however, was ultimately unsuccessful as several states continued the legal battle, leading to a federal jury finding Live Nation liable for operating an illegal monopoly.
